sections.h2: How big is Jefferson County, Georgia, and who lives there?
sections.html:
Jefferson County is wide and sparsely populated: 530 square miles, 526 of them land, with 29.8 people per square mile in 2020. Louisville is the seat and the largest of five cities that also include Avera, Stapleton, Wadley and Wrens. The legislature established the county on February 20, 1796, per Wikipedia.

Its neighbors are McDuffie, Richmond, Burke, Emanuel, Johnson, Glascock, Washington and Warren. Streams south of a line running southeast from Stapleton, just below State Route 80, empty into the Upper Ogeechee; the small area north of it belongs to Brier Creek and the Savannah system. One county school district covers the whole county. The 2020 census counted every resident as rural and put the median age at 43.4.

QuickFacts has 22.4% of residents at 65 or older and 21.3% under 18, with 5,751 households of 2.58 people each. The poverty rate is 21.5% and 13.5% of adults hold a bachelor's degree. In 2023 the county had 326 employer establishments and 4,046 jobs.

sections.h2: What is a Jefferson County house worth, and is the market growing?
sections.html:
Values are low and the headcount is falling. The middle value of an owned home is $105,400 for 2020-2024, and the July 2025 estimate of 15,011 residents sits 4.5% under the April 2020 base.

The county held 18,403 people in 1980 and 16,930 in 2010. The 2020 census found 7,148 housing units, with 13.7% vacant. Competition for a buyer comes largely from other older houses, and one carrying no delinquent years is the easier one to place.

sections.h2: Where do I take Jefferson County tax questions?
sections.html:
Bills and payments belong to the Tax Commissioner, 736 Peachtree Street, Louisville, GA 30434, telephone (478) 625-7736, weekdays from 8:30 until 5:00. Values belong to the Tax Assessor at (478) 625-8209.

  • Tax Commissioner: real property, personal property, motor vehicle, mobile home and timber bills
  • Board of Tax Assessors: takes returns, homestead forms and appeals
  • Clerk of Superior Court: warranty deed copies from its record center, and the FANS alert service; the county tax site gives the clerk at (478) 625-7922

County commissioners and the school board decide millage. The Tax Commissioner has no say over value or rate.

sections.h2: What happens if I miss the Jefferson County deadline?
sections.html:
The usual deadline for real estate and business personal property is November 15, and 90 days later a 10% penalty arrives. Homesteaded property with a bill under $500 is spared that penalty.

Beyond that, unpaid tax gives the Tax Commissioner both the right and the duty to levy on the property. The office calls that a last resort and says it prefers other collection methods.

  • Mobile and modular homes list April 1 on one county page and May 1 on another, so ask which date applies to you
  • A mobile home location permit requires the year's tax to be paid in full
  • Vehicle tax follows the owner's birthday

The tax site also mentions a one-time state homestead relief grant shown as a line on bills for owners with an approved exemption. Rentals and non-homesteaded property did not qualify.

sections.h2: How do returns and homestead applications work in Jefferson County?
sections.html:
Everyone owning taxable property on January 1 must file at least a first return, between January 1 and April 1. A real property return then renews itself yearly at last year's value until you add property or improve it.

Personal property works differently. The PT-50P form goes to the Board of Assessors every year, and anything you no longer own must be reported to the assessor or you will still be taxed on it. A fresh return declaring a lower value, filed in the window, starts your appeal if the assessors turn it down.

  • New homeowners should carry a copy of their warranty deed to the Tax Assessor's Office
  • Forms are taken year round, but a form received after April 1 counts for the next tax year
  • A granted exemption continues until you move, transfer title or ask for a different type
  • A denial must be sent to you in writing and can be appealed

A larger local exemption beats the State's. Ask the assessor's office what the combined amounts are.

sections.h2: How can I appeal a Jefferson County value?
sections.html:
Send the Board of Tax Assessors a written appeal after you receive notice of a change in value. The county's general page says 45 days from mailing, while its FAQ says 30 days, so go by the notice in your hand and file early.

Grounds are taxability, value and uniformity with similar parcels. The size of your tax bill is not a ground. The assessors take a second look, then tell you their decision; if you still disagree, your file moves to the County Board of Equalization for a hearing, and Superior Court is the next level. Arbitration is offered as an alternative to the board, and the Board of Tax Assessors can explain how to elect it.

sections.h2: Which farm, timber and historic programs apply in Jefferson County?
sections.html:
Land used for real farming can be assessed at 30% of market value instead of the usual 40%. A second route, conservation use, values qualifying farm, timber, sensitive or transitional land by what it is used for today.

  • Covenant: the owner commits to the Board of Tax Assessors to keep the land in that use for at least 10 years, and applications are due in April
  • Standing timber: untaxed until sold or cut, then taxed at full market value times the millage rate
  • Historic buildings: a register-listed structure and up to two surrounding acres can get preferential treatment

If you own acreage, talk to the assessor before listing so you know what the covenant requires of a new owner.

sections.h2: How do I clear tax before a Jefferson County closing?
sections.html:
Ask the Tax Commissioner for the payoff in writing and settle it at the closing table. Once a bill is more than 90 days old, the 10% penalty has been added, and the office can levy on the property.

The Clerk of Superior Court offers FANS, a free opt-in service that emails or texts you when records are filed against your property. Sign up before listing so a surprise lien does not appear mid-contract. If you inherited the house or kept it as a rental, ask for each earlier year's balance on its own.

faqs.q: When is the Jefferson County tax bill due?
faqs.a: Generally November 15 for real estate and business personal property. A 10% penalty applies after 90 more days.

faqs.q: Which phone reaches the Jefferson County Tax Commissioner?
faqs.a: (478) 625-7736, at 736 Peachtree Street in Louisville. Weekday hours run from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

faqs.q: Do small homesteaded bills pay a penalty in Jefferson County?
faqs.a: No. A homesteaded property with a bill under $500 is exempt from the 90-day penalty.

faqs.q: By what date must a Jefferson County owner apply for homestead?
faqs.a: April 1. Applications are accepted all year, but a later one starts with the next tax year.

faqs.q: Whom do I ask about a Jefferson County value?
faqs.a: The Tax Assessor, at (478) 625-8209. The Tax Commissioner handles billing and payments.
